children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Eicher Motors on Friday reported a 15% year-on-year increase in second-quarter consolidated net profit as costs from rising raw materials offset gains from strong motorcycle sales. September-quarter consolidated net profit stood at 1,573 crore, below analysts' estimates. Analysts had estimated consolidated net profit of 1,626 crore, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company's revenue from operations rose 20% year-on-year to 7,422 crore.

Ebitda (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) for the quarter grew by 16% to a record 1,760 crore compared with 1,512 crore a year ago. Eicher Motors' flagship motorcycle brand Royal Enfield recorded its highest-ever quarterly sales of 376,722 units, up 15% from 327,067 a year ago. "Q2 of FY27 has been the best-ever quarter for Eicher Motors, with both Royal Enfield and VECV delivering solid performances," said B Govindarajan, managing director, Eicher Motors, and chief executive officer, Royal Enfield. "At Royal Enfield, the robust demand across domestic and key international markets drove our highest-ever quarterly and festive wholesales across September and October." Govindarajan said the company's international markets, too, continued to grow, supported by new motorcycle launches.

Expenses last quarter went up nearly 22% on the back of higher input costs. The company raised prices of Royal Enfield motorcycles by 1.75% earlier this year to offset these costs. VE Commercial Vehicles' revenue from operations last quarter stood at 7,569 crore, up 24% from 6,106 crore a year ago. Ebitda for the Q2 rose 23% to 588 crore from 479 crore a year ago. Profit after tax stood at 342 crore vs 249 crore last year. VECV recorded sales of 28,071 vehicles in Q2, up 28.2% from 21,901 vehicles in the previous year.

title: Eicher Motors Q2 Net Rises 15%, But Misses Estimates
